title: Outbound URL fetches can bypass private-host protections

evidence.quote: if not url.startswith("http"): ... response = await client.get(url)

reasoning: The reader validates only the initial URL, then enables automatic redirects and consumes the final response without validating the redirected host. A public URL that redirects to loopback, link-local, or another private address will still be fetched. The YouTube channel resolver is stricter in name than behavior: any already-http URL is fetched directly with redirects enabled and no public-host validation at all. Both paths accept user-controlled URLs and can make the server connect to internal services.
reproduction: Serve a public HTTP URL that returns a 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:8080/ and pass it to reader mode, or POST an internal URL to /youtube/resolve. The server attempts the internal request before returning an error or parsed result.
recommendation: Disable automatic redirects for SSRF-sensitive fetches and follow redirects manually only after validating each Location with the same public-host policy. For YouTube channel resolution, reject non-YouTube hosts before any request and still validate redirects.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests cover transcription and YouTube video URL extraction only; there are no reader fetch or YouTube channel resolver tests for private hosts, redirects, or non-YouTube URLs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add async tests that mock a public URL redirecting to localhost and assert fetch_html_document rejects it before fetching the private response; add a /youtube/resolve or resolver test that rejects http://127.0.0.1 and non-youtube.com hosts.
minimumFixScope: app/services/reader_service.py and app/services/youtube_channel_resolver.py, with focused tests for redirect and host validation.

history.reasoning: The original evidence paths still exist, but the vulnerable behavior no longer matches current code. app/services/reader_service.py now disables automatic redirects with follow_redirects=False and manually validates the initial URL, each current_url before fetch, and each redirect Location via validate_public_url before continuing. app/services/youtube_channel_resolver.py now normalizes/rejects non-YouTube URLs before opening an HTTP client, uses follow_redirects=False, and validates redirect targets through _normalize_youtube_url before following them. app/api/media.py still passes user input to resolve_youtube_channel, but the resolver now rejects non-YouTube/private redirect targets before fetching them. Current regression tests exist in tests/test_reader_service.py and tests/test_youtube_channel_resolver.py for private redirect blocking and non-YouTube rejection. Pytest could not start in this read-only sandbox because Python/pytest had no usable temporary directory, but an inline Python regression check mirroring those tests passed and confirmed no fetch of the private redirect target occurs.
commands: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -c '<inline manual SSRF regression checks for reader private redirect, YouTube non-YouTube rejection, and YouTube private redirect>'
